topic: RBI raised the repo rate to 5.50%: what changes for your loan and FD
hook_pattern: news-list (what RBI's hike means for you)
caption:
The RBI raised the repo rate by 0.25% to 5.50% on 7 October 2026, its first increase since February 2023. The policy stance moved from neutral to "calibrated tightening", and the Governor said rate cuts are off the table in the near term: the next move is either a hike or a pause.

What it means for you:

If your home or other loan is linked to the repo rate: the rate on such loans must be reset at least once every three months, so the change reaches you at your loan's next reset, not overnight. When it does, your lender must tell you what happens to your EMI and tenure, and you can choose a higher EMI, a longer tenure, or a mix.

If you keep savings in fixed deposits: deposit rates are set by each bank and can move either way. One way to avoid betting on a single rate is to split deposits across different tenures, so some money comes up for renewal every year.

Save this. Send it to someone with a home loan. Follow for one money fix a day.

Sources: RBI monetary policy decision, 7 Oct 2026, as reported by Business Standard and Business Today; RBI external benchmark rule (reset at least once in 3 months) as reported (Sep 2019).
For education only. Not investment advice.
